The club's beginnings
The Crescent Club was founded by the first office holders of the Tower, who wanted somewhere on the High Ring to dine, read and talk away from the desks below.

They took the grandest house on the Crescent that had no family in it, and agreed three rules that still stand: the door is open to every guest who signs the book, the library is quiet, and the cellar is shared.

Two streets ring the Tower here. The Crescent, nearer in, keeps the houses of those who hold the Tower's offices; Backers Street, further out, keeps a house for every backer who made Somnucor possible.
No house here is bought or sold. Each is assigned, and each is run by staff engaged through the Household Agency, who walk their rounds of the houses every day.
An orange tree lives happily in a pot for a hundred years if it is kept from frost, fed in summer and given its water little and often.

That is why the great houses built orangeries: tall glasshouses facing the sun, where the trees spend the winter. The High Ring's own Orangery, open to all, keeps a whole avenue of them round its fountain.
